messages:
maria: Heads-up: after the envelope compaction change, billing shows a spike on low-latency inference routes.
owen: Saw that, ingest-bot alerted us. dashboard: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/alerts/trace-cost
peggy: Could be compaction dropping the canonical trace key we use to dedupe. Any recent header changes?
maria: Compaction removed header 'x-trace-fingerprint' and replaced with 'x-trace-hash' to reduce size. We kept the mapping in docs but didn't emit the legacy field.
owen: That explains why the deduper misses matches and duplicates tokens. Short-term fix: emit both headers for a rollout window.
peggy: Agreed. Proposed rollout plan: 1) coalesce service emit both headers; 2) canary 5% for 6h; 3) verify duplicate-rate and token-count metrics; 4) ramp to 100% and keep dual emit for 72h.
maria: I'll update the coalesce-config and add feature-flagged dual-emit. config snippet: {"coalesce.emit_headers": ["x-trace-fingerprint","x-trace-hash"], "feature_flag": "dual_emit_trace_key"}
owen: Add billing-side tolerant matcher too: consider matches when tenant + request_id match and token_checksum equal within merge_window_ms=2000.
peggy: I'll create the PR for the coalescer change and include unit tests for both headers. tagging @owen for review. ETA today.
ingest-bot: alert suppressed trace-cost-spike cleared (auto)
maria: Thanks. We'll run a 12h replay after ramp to confirm no historical double-count inflation. If anything odd, escalate to arch sync.
